_note: The v2 pool-size sweep (issue #51, widened to 2k-10k at 1k steps by Jahid on 2026-10-14; shape fixed in ADR 0035). ONE factor moves: pool size. Everything else is exp-020's arm (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, 4-bit, unguided, ADR 0007 pinned 600, imbalanced construction per ADR 0031 item 1, e5-small-v2 top-20 -> ms-marco cross-encoder rerank -> top-5, seed 42). This file is read by the experiment-runner, not by a script: it names the sizes, every flag of every stage, and the sha256 each prebuilt input must have, so a run can be checked against it before launch. It is deliberately separate from configs/pool_sweep.json, which drives scripts/pool_sweep_orchestrator.py's full construction x mode x retriever cross - widening that file's imbalanced_sizes would make the orchestrator re-run the v1-shaped matrix ADR 0035 rules out. {size} and {exp_id} are the only template fields; paths are relative to the repo root of the main checkout.
_exp_id_note: Next free id when this file was written (exp-029 is the concurrent CPU re-analysis). The experiment-runner confirms it against experiments/log.md and writes the log row before launch; if the id has been taken, use the next free one and substitute it everywhere {exp_id} appears.

pool._nesting_note: The imbalanced strategy is Python's random.Random(42).sample(rows, size) over all 19,938 enriched train rows. random.sample picks its algorithm from the requested size: for size <= 5461 it uses the set-based method, for size >= 5462 (n=19938 <= 21 + 4**ceil(log4(3*size))) the pool-swap method. Each method is prefix-consistent, so the pools form TWO nested chains, not one: 2k c 3k c 4k c 5k (each the exact prefix of the next) and 6k c 7k c 8k c 9k c 10k (likewise), but 5k is NOT a subset of 6k - they share 3,553 of 5,000 ids - and 2k shares 1,946 of its 2,000 ids with 10k. The 5k->6k step therefore changes the draw as well as the size. Measured 2026-10-14 (ml-engineer, issue #51 prep).

nested_extension._note: Lead decision 2026-10-14 under Jahid delegation (ADR 0035 amendment): ONE nested chain anchored on the adopted 2k pool. 2k-5k come from sample_pool.py as in pool.command_template (exact prefixes of one random.sample draw). 6k-10k come from scripts/extend_pool_nested.py: the 5k pool plus a prefix of the remaining input rows, sorted by id then shuffled once with seed. Paths base_pool/out_root are relative to the runs root of configs/paths.json.

retrieval.cache: disabled (--no-cache): every size's pool embeddings are computed fresh, so no artifact depends on an embedding-cache entry of unknown provenance, and nothing is written into the v1 cache directory the data root symlinks to

decompose._note: exp-020's step_1 command with only --retrieval-input and --output-root moved. --quantization 4bit and --retrieval-input are passed explicitly (configs/decomposer_musique.json _runnable_models_note; the model folder default stays quantization none). few_shot.ordering stays at the config default as_is, which is the behaviour exp-020 ran under (it predates the key).

compare._note: Each size against the 2k point with the evaluator's battery (ADR 0009); no multiple-comparison correction unless a slide states Holm (ADR 0035). The 2k point is this sweep's own 2k re-run (see reproducibility_gate_2k), so every pair is same-run, same-code, same eval set. The extra pair 2k-rerun vs exp-020 measures whether re-generating the 2k arm reproduces exp-020.
compare.pairs: size{size} vs size2000 for size in sizes[1:] (8 pairs)

reproducibility_gate_2k.verdict: FAIL on the sha256 rule - the sweep re-runs 2k; exp-020 is not reused as the 2k point
reproducibility_gate_2k.pool: MATCH: rebuilt size2000 pool sha256 cc3646625d759a1b58179b18c25f83d255db24f05acc08b666985af2e58d6646 = exp-020/exp-014 input, 2000 rows, 1461/413/126
reproducibility_gate_2k.retrieval: NO MATCH: rebuilt top-20 sha256 15adefdf... vs exp-014 493360b4...; rebuilt rerank top-5 sha256 bbbdb63f... vs exp-014/exp-020 3f95c7dc.... The difference is ROW ORDER ONLY: keyed by query_id, all 600 rows of both stages are identical in every field (same top-k ids, same scores, same masked query). Cause: the three pinned-600 query files under musique/dev_data were rewritten on 2026-09-14 15:01 (mtime), after exp-014 (2026-08-23); they hold the same 600 ids in a different order, and the retrieval scripts write rows in query-file order.
reproducibility_gate_2k.why_rerun_anyway: ADR 0035 makes byte identity the rule. Re-running 2k also puts all nine sizes on the same code, the same day and the same input order, and the extra compare (2k re-run vs exp-020) measures whether re-generating the arm reproduces exp-020.

_expected_inputs_note: sha256 of every prebuilt input, built 2026-10-14 on the commands above (pool and retrieval, --device cpu, --no-cache, seed 42). Before launching a size, recompute the sha256 of its pool.jsonl and pinned600_imbalanced_rerank_top5.jsonl and refuse to run on a mismatch. Every pool has 0 id overlap and 0 exact question-text overlap with the pinned 600; every retrieval file has 600 rows (200/200/200), the pinned-600 id set exactly, k=20 / k=5 per row, and no candidate outside its own pool.
